458	      terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1);

468	    const handleTransitionEnd = (e: TransitionEvent) => {
469	      if (cancelled) return;
470	      if (e.target === container.parentElement) {
471	        resizeAttempts = 0;
472	        lastHeight = -1;
473	        setTimeout(() => {
474	          if (!cancelled) rafId = requestAnimationFrame(resizeTerminal);
475	        }, 50);
476	      }
477	    };
478	
479	    const parent = container.parentElement;
480	    parent?.addEventListener("transitionend", handleTransitionEnd);
481	
482	    // Backup timers in case RAF polling doesn't work
483	    const timer1 = setTimeout(() => {
484	      if (cancelled) return;
485	      resizeAttempts = 0;
486	      lastHeight = -1;

492	      lastHeight = -1;
493	      resizeTerminal();
494	    }, 600);
495	
496	    return () => {
497	      cancelled = true;
498	      cancelAnimationFrame(rafId);
499	      parent?.removeEventListener("transitionend", handleTransitionEnd);
500	      clearTimeout(timer1);
501	      clearTimeout(timer2);

how do we test dry installation using pnpm? I would like to manually mk sure that the warning is gone.

> AGENT

To check for deprecation warnings without modifying anything:

```bash
pnpm install --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -i "deprecated\|warn"
```

Or for a fresh resolution that shows all warnings:

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 2>&1 | grep -i "deprecated\|warn"
```

The original deprecation warning came from the old `xterm` package (the unscoped one). Since the previous commit already migrated to `@xterm/xterm` and you've now bumped to v6, you can also just check what's in the lockfile:

```bash
grep "xterm" pnpm-lock.yaml | grep -v "^#"
```

That'll confirm only `@xterm/xterm@6.0.0` and the addons appear — no unscoped `xterm` entry. That's the cleanest indicator without a full install.

No dry-run equivalent exists. The closest option is `--lockfile-only` — it resolves dependencies and updates `pnpm-lock.yaml` without downloading anything to `node_modules`. But your lockfile is already updated from the install we ran earlier.

The simplest way to verify the warning without a full reinstall is just to grep the lockfile directly:

```bash
grep "xterm" pnpm-lock.yaml
```

If you see only `@xterm/xterm@6.0.0` and no `xterm@5` or the unscoped `xterm`, the deprecated package is gone.
